subject: Controlling for variable effort in spAbundance - transect.lenghts vs offset

messages.author: f18889d55d3eefd9
messages.subject: Controlling for variable effort in spAbundance - transect.lenghts vs offset
parts:
Hello!

I'm using the distance sampling function in spAbundance to get transect-level yearly estimates for a 20 year dataset. I've formatted my data so that every row is a transect-year combination and am including year as a covariate in my models to get at overall trends. 
The transects in this case consist of points along a line where point counts were conducted, and in some years not all points were visited. I want to account for this variation in effort and have a few questions:
1. If I supply transect.lengths a vector with the length of each transect that was surveyed, will that effectively take care of effort?
2. Am I correct in thinking that if no offset is supplied, the output will be number of individuals per transect? (or in my case transect-year)
3. I would ultimately like the output to be density per square km to be consistent with prior reports - in order to do this would I have to provide a vector of offset values before fitting models (and what would those be in relation to transect lengths?) or alternatively would I manipulate the model output (N.samples?) to calculate density post hoc?

Thanks a lot!!
Taylor

messages.author: 0b274a0ee3490d75
messages.subject: Re: Controlling for variable effort in spAbundance - transect.lenghts vs offset
parts:
Hi Taylor, 

Thanks for the question, and sorry for the long delay. Here are some thoughts on your design which I think might answer all three questions. 

From my understanding, you are working with point count data, where the points counts were distributed along transects, but the distance sampling was done within the individual point count locations. If that is correct, I would suggest modeling the data at the individual point count level such that each row is a point count-year combination. You would then set transect = "point" and offset = the area (in km2) of the point count survey region over which distances were recorded. When doing this, the estimates from mu.samples would be in terms of density (i.e., individuals per km^2), while N.samples would be a per-point/year abundance estimate. See the vignette for some more details on the statistical notation for that. If you model at the point-year level, this automatically will account for uneven sampling across years because years in which a given point is not measured simply will not be included in the data set. Also, if you model at the point-level you will want to include a transect-level random effect (i.e., (1 | transect)) and potentially a point count level random effect to account for the repeat measurements of the individual locations over time. If no offset is supplied in this case, then the output will be in terms of number of individuals per point-year. If you did the distance sampling within individual point counts that were clustered together on transects and then tried to model at the transect level, it would be very challenging to define a detection function that made sense. The "transect" term in spAbundance refers to a situation in which distance sampling is conducted by walking along a transect and recording distances to individuals within some band of the transect line. This differs from what I assume your case is, where individual points are where the distance sampling is done and the point locations were sampled to fall along transects. 

Hope that helps. Let me know if I interpreted anything about your data set incorrectly. 

Jeff
